scope: Matched DLAYL Y/N on a genuine lateral peer with an item in scheduled transit at the demand time
manual_basis: LateralSupport.DLAYL allows considering lateral support when no peer has a free item now but one will soon be available (manual p320). ItemTransfer BETWEEN schedules physical stock with a positive TFDT; accepted I02.var04 observed delayed physical arrival.
controlled_design: From accepted E08 ENLAT=Y IMMEDIATE source, change peer BASE-02 STSIZ1→0 and add one scheduled ItemTransfer BETWEEN of depot physical ID0 to peer at h9 with TFDT2, so it is in transit at BASE-01's h10 ordinary demand and scheduled to arrive peer h11. Keep depot initial stock1, base initial0, one IID, LAT-01, half-hour lateral transport, one-hour ordinary item downward transport, TRACK=Y, half-hour ITEM collection, seed1 and horizon36. The two child arms differ only DLAYL N/Y and descriptive text.
pre_run_hypotheses: Both arms import and exactly roundtrip 25 populated authored tables, convert with zero errors and yield nonempty native output.
The scheduled h9 transfer moves physical depot ID0 toward BASE-02 and arrives at h11, so the peer has no on-hand spare at the h10 BASE-01 shortage but a known future arrival.

With DLAYL=Y, the h10 shortage may reserve that future peer item for lateral shipment after its h11 arrival; with DLAYL=N, it may wait for ordinary support. The native event log and station ledgers, not the hypothesis, determine acceptance.
Transfer backorder, peer/ordinary backorder, item identities, arrivals, aircraft readiness, mission effects and terminal stock must reconcile in each arm.
acceptance_gate: A positive DLAYL comparison requires the h9 transfer to execute and remain in transit at h10, the Y/N source contrast to be isolated, and a native physical-route or wait-time difference attributable to the switch. If Y/N behave alike, publish only a reproducible limitation or counterexample with the observed sequence; if the transfer or reporting fails, retain diagnostic only.
limits: one scheduled BETWEEN supply in transit toward an empty peer
one IID, depot and peer, immediate lateral rule, fixed seed
no general future-supply sources, priority, deeper chains, GUI rendering or cross-engine parity
